notes: Hand-canonicalised from the structured extraction in lp2graph/corpus/Gurobi__modeling-examples.json; the automatic converter refuses this model (see _report.json: 'sum binder \{i,j\} \subseteq S maps to no declared index family').

Excluded row 'resource_capacity_hotspot': the hotspot cut sum_{{i,j} subset S} x_{i,j,r} <= C(c_r+1,2)-1 binds a sum over subsets of a set and is outside the canonical grammar. The capacity parameter c_r is therefore not declared here; unit-capacity resources are covered by 'unit_capacity'.

Index family R is declared ordered so that r+1 denotes the next resource of the route under consideration; 'first', 'last' and 'single' are 0/1 attributes read by quantifier where-predicates, matching the source's per-route first/last resource and its capacity-1 resources.
Source model row 'conflict_meet_pair' is a conjunction of two inequalities; only the first is carried here, as 'conflict_meet'.
Used as the worked example of the Paper-1 figure fig:anatomy; every claim in that figure is checked by scripts/checks/anatomy_figure_check.py.

Grounds and solves: cardinalities I=2, R=3, dur=[2,3,2], first=[1,0,0], last=[0,0,1], single=[0,1,0], M=1000 -> status optimal under both CBC and HiGHS, schedule t[1]=(0,2,5) tF[1]=7 (leader), t[0]=(0,5,8) tF[0]=10 (follower waits for the unit-capacity middle resource); Sum tF = 17 is the true minimum.

Library defect FIXED (lp2graph 03316fe, issue #60, ADR-0016): the grounder used to derive a sum's loops from the term's bindings only and ignored Term.operator_over, so 'sum_{i in I, r in R} dur_r' grounded to sum_r dur_r and the reported objective was 10.0. It now grounds to |I| * sum_r dur_r: objective 3.0 under both CBC and HiGHS (17 - 2 * 7), the value the algebra states; the schedule is unchanged.
